title.narrative: Cote d'Ivoire Higher Education Development Support Project

description.narrative: The Project Development Objectives are: (a) improve higher education management; (b) increase enrollment in professional programs; (c) improve the quality and labor market relevance of degree programs of participating public tertiary institutions.

The development objective of Higher Education Development Support Project for Côte d'Ivoire are: (a) improve higher education management; (b) increase enrollment in professional programs; (c) improve the quality and labor market relevance of degree programs of participating public tertiary institutions. 1) The first component, Strengthening Tertiary Education Management, aims to support the government as it modernizes governance of tertiary education by giving individual institutions higher level of autonomy. It has the following subcomponents: (i) Supporting the establishment of a Performance-based Contracts system of sub grants; (ii) Reinforcing Education Sector Management Capacity; (iii) Establishing a new Quality Assurance System; and (iv) Project Management. 2) The second component, Enhancing Short Duration Professional Programs, aims to make short duration tertiary programs more effective in order to help increase graduate employment. It has the following subcomponents: (i) Creation of Higher Institutes of Professional Training and Technology; and (ii) Reviewing and Upgrading Higher Technician Certificate. 3) The third component, Enhancing Graduates Employability in Public Universities and National Polytechnique Institute Houphouët-Boigny (INPHB), aims to help public tertiary institutions make the transition to the LMD system and support measures to enhance the quality and relevance of their programs. It has the following subcomponents: (i) Improving the Quality and Relevance of Public University Programs; and (ii) Upgrading the INPHB.

condition.narrative: Section I.A.3 (d) (i). The Recipient shall, through the PIU no later than one (1) month after the Effective Date: appoint afinancial controller, a public accountant, a procurement specialist, and a monitoring and evaluation specialist.

Section I.A.3 (d) (ii). The Recipient shall, through the PIU no later than two (2) months after the Effective Date recruit anaccountant and an assistant accountant, acquire and install an accounting software.
Section I.A.3 (d) (iii). The Recipient shall, through the PIU no later than five (5) months after the Effective Date appoint anexternal auditor.

Section I.F (2). The Recipient shall ensure that the obligation to comply with the relevant Safeguard Instruments is incorporated:(a) in all Performance-based Contracts; (b) in the contracts between the Recipient and its contractors and any entity supervisingthe Project's civil works; and (c) in the contracts between the contractors and any of their subcontractors.

Section I.F (3). The Recipient shall ensure that all bidding documents and contracts for civil works include the obligation of therelevant contractors and subcontractors to adopt and implement measures to assess and manage the risks and impacts of labor influxand workers camps.

Section I.F (4). The Recipient shall ensure that all contracts for civil works under the Project obligate the applicablecontractors and subcontractors to: (a) adopt and enforce a code of conduct that applies to and is signed by all personnel workingon any Project activities, in form and substance acceptable to the Association, detailing measures on environmental, health andsafety as well as measures to prevent and respond to GBV; (b) report promptly to the PIU any allegations of GBV against any oftheir personnel; and (c) investigate promptly and thoroughly any allegations of violations of said code of conduct.

Section I.F (8). The Recipient shall ensure that: (a) all consultancies related to technical assistance, design and capacitybuilding under the Project, the application of whose results could have environmental, social and health and safety implications,shall only be undertaken pursuant to terms of reference reviewed and found satisfactory by the Association; and (b) such terms ofreference shall require the technical assistance, design and capacity building activities to take into account the requirements ofthe applicable Safeguards Policies and EHS Guidelines.

title.narrative: Percentage of public universities supported by the project having an internal QA unit

comment.narrative: The QA system is not in place yet. The adoption of the legal text for the creation of the National Agency for Quality Assurance (ANAQ) is expected after the adoption of the law by the parliament. Therefore Universities are drafting the necessary documents to be ready once the law is adopted.
The 2021/2022 statistical yearbook is published and available.
